lessons.title: System Databases: master, msdb, model & tempdb

slots.practicalActivity: On a local SQL Server instance, query sys.databases to list master, msdb, model, and tempdb alongside any user databases and their recovery models, then query sys.tables and sys.objects against AdventureWorks2012 to see how catalog views expose schema metadata, and run a first DMV query against sys.dm_exec_sessions to list currently connected sessions and their login names.
slots.deliverable: A saved .sql script with three working queries — one against sys.databases, one against sys.tables/sys.objects in AdventureWorks2012, and one against sys.dm_exec_sessions — each with a one-line comment explaining what it reveals.

slots.practicalActivity: Query SERVERPROPERTY() for edition, version, and collation, and DATABASEPROPERTYEX() for AdventureWorks2012's recovery model and collation; then query sys.dm_exec_connections joined to sys.dm_exec_sessions to list every current connection's login name, host name, and program name.
slots.deliverable: A .sql script with a server-properties query, a database-properties query, and a sessions/connections query, each returning real values from the local instance.

lessons.title: Monitoring CPU, Memory & I/O With T-SQL

slots.practicalActivity: Query sys.dm_os_performance_counters and sys.dm_os_sys_info for CPU/memory signals, then sys.dm_exec_query_stats joined to sys.dm_exec_sql_text to rank the 10 most CPU-expensive cached queries, and sys.dm_os_wait_stats to find the top 5 wait types by wait_time_ms on the instance.
slots.deliverable: A single .sql script with three labeled sections — resource counters, top 10 expensive queries, and top 5 waits — runnable in one pass against the local instance.

slots.practicalActivity: Open two SSMS sessions against AdventureWorks2012: in session A, start an explicit BEGIN TRAN that updates a row in Person.Person without committing; in session B, run a SELECT against that same row to create real blocking. In a third session, run the sys.dm_exec_requests.blocking_session_id query and the recursive chain-walking query from the lesson to identify the root blocker, then query sys.dm_db_file_space_usage for current tempdb space.
slots.deliverable: A short write-up (3-4 sentences) naming the blocked session_id, the blocking_session_id, and the wait_resource you observed, plus the tempdb space-usage query output.

slots.practicalActivity: Combine Chapter 2 into one standing monitoring script: resource counters, top expensive queries, top waits, blocking chains, and tempdb space, each as a clearly labeled section you could run as a first-response health check on any unfamiliar server.
slots.deliverable: A single saved monitoring.sql script with five labeled sections (counters, expensive queries, waits, blocking, tempdb/space) that runs clean start to finish on the local instance.

slots.practicalActivity: Run sys.dm_db_index_physical_stats against AdventureWorks2012 to list every index's avg_fragmentation_in_percent and page_count, then query sys.dm_db_missing_index_details/_group_stats and sys.dm_db_index_usage_stats to find one genuinely unused index (high writes, zero or near-zero seeks) and one duplicate-candidate index on the same table.
slots.deliverable: A short findings table listing one fragmented index, one missing-index suggestion, and one unused/duplicate index, each with the DMV columns that justify the finding.

lessons.title: When Not to Rebuild an Index

slots.practicalActivity: Query sys.dm_db_stats_properties joined to sys.stats on a Sales.SalesOrderDetail-sized table to check rows_sampled vs. rows and modification_counter, run UPDATE STATISTICS on one stale statistic, and then decide — using the fragmentation numbers and page_count from the previous slot — which index should be REORGANIZEd, which should be REBUILT, and which is too small (low page_count) to bother with at all.
slots.deliverable: A written decision table: index name, fragmentation %, page count, and your REORGANIZE/REBUILD/skip verdict with a one-line reason for each.

slots.practicalActivity: Query sys.dm_tran_active_transactions and sys.dm_tran_session_transactions to list every open transaction and how long it's been open, then query sys.dm_tran_locks to see the actual lock resources and modes held by a transaction you deliberately leave open (BEGIN TRAN, no COMMIT) in a second session.
slots.deliverable: A .sql script with the open-transactions query and the sys.dm_tran_locks query, plus the actual lock mode/resource output captured from your deliberately-opened transaction.

slots.practicalActivity: Set SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL READ COMMITTED vs. SERIALIZABLE in two sessions reading/writing the same AdventureWorks2012 rows and observe the blocking difference, then deliberately reproduce a deadlock (two sessions updating two rows in opposite order) and capture the deadlock graph from the system_health extended events session.
slots.deliverable: A short report naming which isolation level produced more blocking, plus the captured deadlock graph (XML export or screenshot) identifying both the victim and the survivor session.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a reusable transactions-and-deadlocks toolkit: one query for open transactions, one for current blocking chains, and one for pulling the most recent deadlock graph out of system_health — with a comment on when a DBA would reach for each one.
slots.deliverable: A saved blocking-and-deadlocks.sql file with three labeled, independently runnable sections.

slots.practicalActivity: Against a test database set to FULL recovery, run BACKUP DATABASE WITH COMPRESSION, CHECKSUM, make a change, run BACKUP DATABASE WITH DIFFERENTIAL, make another change, run BACKUP LOG, then RESTORE the full backup WITH NORECOVERY, the differential WITH NORECOVERY, and the log backup WITH RECOVERY, STOPAT set to a timestamp just before your last change.
slots.deliverable: The complete restore script (full to differential to log WITH STOPAT) plus confirmation that the restored database is missing only the change made after your STOPAT timestamp.

slots.practicalActivity: Run RESTORE VERIFYONLY against each backup file from the previous slot to confirm they're readable and not corrupt, then query msdb.dbo.backupset and msdb.dbo.backupmediafamily to build a report of every backup taken for that database in the last 24 hours, including backup type, size, and physical device path.
slots.deliverable: A backup-history report query against msdb showing backup_start_date, type, and physical_device_name for every backup taken in this slot and the previous one.

slots.practicalActivity: Run a full disaster-recovery drill end to end on a disposable test database: take full, differential, and log backups, intentionally DROP the database, restore it completely from that backup chain (running RESTORE VERIFYONLY first on each file), and confirm row counts on at least one table match the pre-drop values.
slots.deliverable: A disaster-recovery-drill.sql script covering backup, drop, verify, and restore, plus a before/after row-count comparison proving the restore was complete.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a new SQL login and a corresponding database user in AdventureWorks2012, add the user to db_datareader, GRANT SELECT explicitly on one additional table, DENY SELECT on one sensitive column via a view, and then REVOKE the db_datareader membership to observe the access change take effect.
slots.deliverable: A security-setup.sql script creating the login/user and running the GRANT/DENY/REVOKE statements in order, with a one-line note on what access the user had at each step.

slots.practicalActivity: Query sys.database_principals joined against sys.server_principals to find any orphaned database users in AdventureWorks2012, then run a security-audit query against sys.server_permissions, sys.database_permissions, and sys.server_role_members to list every login with sysadmin or an equivalent elevated role on the instance.
slots.deliverable: An orphaned-users query output (even if empty, with the query that would catch one) plus a sysadmin/elevated-role audit report naming every principal with high-level access on the instance.

slots.practicalActivity: Package Chapter 6 into a standing security-review script: orphaned users, elevated-role membership, and explicit permission grants/denies on one sensitive table — the kind of script a DBA runs before a compliance audit.
slots.deliverable: A saved security-review.sql file with three labeled sections that runs clean against AdventureWorks2012.

slots.practicalActivity: Query msdb.dbo.sysjobs, sysjobhistory, and sysjobsteps to build a report of every SQL Server Agent job's most recent run outcome, then filter to run_status = 0 to list only failed job steps with their actual error message text from the history.
slots.deliverable: A failed-jobs.sql query returning job name, step name, run date, and error message for any failed job step on the instance (or, if none failed, the same query confirmed working with a note on what it would show).

slots.practicalActivity: Use msdb.dbo.sp_add_job, sp_add_jobstep, and sp_add_jobschedule to create a new Agent job entirely in T-SQL that runs a backup or integrity-check step on a schedule, then use sp_add_operator and sp_add_alert to wire up an email alert tied to a specific error severity level.
slots.deliverable: The full T-SQL script that creates the job, its step, its schedule, an operator, and an alert, plus a query against msdb.dbo.sysjobs confirming the job exists.

slots.practicalActivity: Run DBCC CHECKDB (AdventureWorks2012) WITH NO_INFOMSGS, ALL_ERRORMSGS to get a clean integrity report, then review the allocation-vs-consistency error structure DBCC CHECKDB reports and identify which repair level (REPAIR_REBUILD vs. REPAIR_ALLOW_DATA_LOSS) each error category would require if it appeared.
slots.deliverable: The full DBCC CHECKDB output from a real run against AdventureWorks2012, plus a short note on which repair option you'd reach for given each error type covered in the lesson.

slots.practicalActivity: Query sys.database_files to check each data/log file's current size, autogrowth setting, and growth increment for AdventureWorks2012, then query sys.dm_os_volume_stats joined to sys.database_files to see free space on the underlying volume and calculate an approximate days-until-full at the current growth rate.
slots.deliverable: A capacity-check.sql report showing current file sizes, autogrowth settings, and free volume space, with a one-line projection of runway before manual intervention is needed.

slots.practicalActivity: Enable Query Store on a test database, generate repeated query activity against it, then query sys.query_store_query, sys.query_store_plan, and sys.query_store_runtime_stats to find the top 5 queries by average duration, and separately query sys.dm_exec_cached_plans/sys.dm_exec_query_plan to pull the actual execution plan XML for the worst offender.
slots.deliverable: A Query Store top-5-by-duration report plus the saved execution plan (XML or .sqlplan) for the single worst query you found.

slots.practicalActivity: Run the same parameterized stored procedure first with a highly selective parameter value and then a highly non-selective one, compare the two plans sitting in the plan cache to spot parameter sniffing, then query sys.dm_exec_query_stats to capture current execution counts and average durations as a written performance baseline to compare against later.
slots.deliverable: A short write-up showing the two different plans produced by the same procedure with different parameter values, plus a saved baseline-snapshot.sql query and its output as a reference point.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a performance-troubleshooting toolkit combining the Query Store top-queries report, a plan-cache lookup by query text, and the parameter-sensitivity comparison query into one file a DBA could hand to a teammate during an incident.
slots.deliverable: A saved performance-toolkit.sql file with three labeled, independently runnable sections.

lessons.title: The Toolkit Concept: Reusable, Reliable, Documented
Server Health Check & Database Space Scripts

slots.practicalActivity: Using the toolkit-design principles from the lesson (reusable, reliable, documented), write a server-health-check.sql script combining a server-properties check, a database-space check across all databases, a backup-status check against msdb, and a failed-Agent-jobs check — each section clearly commented with its purpose and what a healthy result looks like.
slots.deliverable: A documented server-health-check.sql file with four labeled, independently runnable sections and a header comment explaining how to run it.

lessons.title: Capstone: Assembling & Presenting Your DBA Toolkit

slots.practicalActivity: Add a blocking-chains section and a long-running-queries section (sessions active longer than a chosen threshold) to the toolkit built in the previous slot, then assemble all five sections — health, space, backups, failed jobs, blocking/long-running — into one final dba-toolkit.sql file with a table-of-contents comment at the top.
slots.deliverable: The final, complete dba-toolkit.sql file with all five sections and a table-of-contents header comment, plus a one-paragraph write-up describing how you'd present this toolkit to a hiring manager.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After this course, a student can use T-SQL alone — DMVs, catalog views, and system procedures — to diagnose blocking, deadlocks, backup/restore gaps, index and statistics problems, and security exposure on a live SQL Server instance, and has assembled those diagnostic queries into a reusable DBA toolkit script.
